newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez falls on Lyonnaise merger news report.
newsitem.headline: Suez falls on Lyonnaise merger news report.

text.p: Shares in holding company Cie de Suez fell heavily on Thursday on the back of a newspaper report saying Lyonnaise des Eaux would absorb Suez through a merger rather than a public share offer, market sources said.

If extraordinary shareholders meetings of the two companies voted a two-thirds majority for a merger, this would rule out Suez' minority shareholders' ability to oppose or negotiate the deal, as might be possible in a public offer.
Suez fell 2.64 percent at 284.3 francs, on volume of 391,256 shares, Lyonnaise was up 1.59 percent at 575, at 1200 GMT.
Suez and Lyonnaise officials were not available for comment.

Market sources estimated that a public offer for Suez would value it close to a net asset value of between 320-340 francs per share and a raised Suez dividend to mollify Cie Generale des Eaux which is hostile to the reported deal.
That compares with a minimum 280 francs per share in a merger deal, reported by newspaper Les Echos.
CGE holds a small Suez stake indirectly through its 20 percent holding in Belgium's Electrabel and is Lyonnaise's main rival in France in the utilities sector.
